chapter: Kid Rena, Kelly and the old trumpeters
title: Chris Kelly, blues trumpeter
summary: Kelly was the favorite blues trumpeter, played growl with derby and plunger, and was heard at Economy Hall.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Do you remember much about Chris Kelly?

Yes I remember a whole lot about Chris Kelly because he used to be the favorite blues trumpet player. I used to like to hear him play the blues more than anybody else. And I just imagine I could see him now playing the blues with perspiration just rolling off his forehead and everything like that.
It was a very picture. I've never even seen a picture of him. How big a fellow was he or what did he look like?
Well let's see, he wasn't too big of a fellow, I don't imagine.
He was as tall as you?
Well I said he would have been taller than I am and a little heavier. I figured maybe about a hundred and seventy, seventy-five pounds like that.
Yes, fairly, not too terribly big. Because I can't remember too much about him because this was a very long time ago and I
was a pretty little fellow, you know? Do you remember did he use mutes or anything or what style of trumpet did he play?

Well he played somewhat of a growl style. They used to use the derbies during them days. Of course the derby hat was very popular. And they'd use the derby and the sink plunger, the plungers that some of the guys use today. They used to use that type of plunger. But very seldom the other mutes style, the cup mutes style. Well it was more or less the plunger and the derby.
Where did you hear Chris Kelly? What sort of places? Was it the halls or?

Well this is at the Economy Hall, I think. I heard him there and I heard him several times on one of these advertisement trucks. I heard him there and I heard him there and he was at one of these famous, what you might call banquets, you used to call a long time ago, Bonquet, which was I think was the Creole pronunciation of it. Yeah. Do you know Creole by the way?
